`Source ((RELATION)) Target` is forward and `Target <((RELATION)) Source` is reverse writing of the same canonical Relation fact. Counts stay on written endpoints; reverse normalization swaps canonical Host/Target and count slots. The declared Relation name is matched exactly. This CFEL operator is distinct from the named graph Relation. It grants no inverse permission and creates no second stored fact.

A CFEL Operator is one declared language component with one token or bounded construct meaning. Each individual operator-instance Declaration supplies its own token semantics. A CFEL Operator is distinct from a graph Relation and does not create a Node, Relation fact, Property occurrence, Carrier fact, or runtime operation. Its declared operator descriptor may be a graph endpoint where a Relation signature admits declared model entities; a glyph or literal operand is not another model entity.
CFEL<+Operator//Name identifies a declared CFEL operator by semantic name.

This CFEL operator binds notation metadata; it does not construct a literal-to-Node graph Relation or equate different Relation identities. The token follows the owning Relation Declaration's directional reading and grants no endpoint permission, cardinality or second authored fact. In a graph expression, `Relation//NAME` references a Relation object as an endpoint, whereas `((NAME))` invokes that Relation between endpoints.
`Operator//Lookup` identifies the declared CFEL value-expression operator. The traversal semantics above are its complete existing contract.

Accept `Node//$x{:1..3}` as a count of the distinct selected logical instances in context, not a one-row count for `$x`; repeated references or Carrier representations of an instance do not multiply the count. Preserve `Kind//{:n}` as a readable historical population selector. Named `Relation//NAME` and `Operator//NAME` addresses and quoted strings retain their identity and text. MODEL Relation descriptor variables stay MODEL evidence; a binder does not create an entity, a Relation fact, an inverse permission or endpoint cardinality.
